raw_plan.interpretation: I interpreted this as one English acquisition email for the qualified slice of the selected audience: devolved and national government digital teams evaluating analytics they can publish without a consent banner. Because the relationship is unknown, the email will introduce Plausible without assuming the recipient uses GA4 or has experienced a migration problem. It will ask for a low-friction evaluation through the live demo.

intent.reason_now: Government digital teams must make an explicit consent decision for analytics tooling, making a documented cookie-free option relevant to evaluate.
intent.desired_action: View Plausible's live example dashboard and decide whether its core reporting is useful enough for a formal assessment.

raw_plan.reader: A member of a devolved or national government digital team responsible for evaluating web analytics against public-sector consent, privacy and reporting requirements.
raw_plan.reader_segment: An EU or UK public sector web team that must publish analytics without a consent banner
raw_plan.reader_scope: Devolved and national government digital teams
raw_plan.promise: Plausible is a concrete cookie-free analytics option to evaluate: it does not use cookies or collect personal data, while its dashboard reports live traffic sources, pages and goals.
raw_plan.orientation: For this team, Plausible is a hosted web analytics service they would name on their published cookies page: it reports traffic sources, pages and goals from one script and one dashboard, and its documentation states it sets no cookies and collects no personal data.
raw_plan.arc: Move the reader from seeing cookie-free analytics as an abstract compliance category to inspecting a working Plausible dashboard and judging whether its core reporting merits formal assessment.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: A single acquisition email should lead with the audience's defining requirement and immediately make the product tangible. The live demo is a lower-friction first step than implementation or account creation and can answer whether the core dashboard is relevant. It cannot settle procurement, legal approval or department-specific reporting requirements, so the email must frame it as an initial evaluation rather than proof of suitability.

emails.selection_reason: The no-cookie design directly matches this audience's consent constraint, while the live dashboard gives an unknown reader a concrete way to determine whether Plausible provides useful core analytics before beginning assurance or procurement work.
emails.job: Get the reader to inspect the live dashboard and decide whether Plausible deserves a formal privacy and reporting assessment.
emails.single_idea: A government web team can evaluate Plausible as a cookie-free analytics option without first taking claims about reporting usefulness on trust: the live dashboard shows the traffic sources, pages and goals it reports.
emails.felt_need: We need useful website analytics without setting non-essential analytics cookies or collecting personal data.
emails.status_quo: Government digital teams commonly operate Google Analytics through Google Tag Manager and document their analytics cookies on public cookies pages.
emails.why_it_fails: Non-essential analytics cookies require prior consent, which conflicts with the requirement to publish analytics without a consent banner.
emails.mechanism: Plausible states that it uses no cookies, collects no personal data, uses no persistent identifiers or cross-site or cross-device tracking, and does not reuse site data. Its dashboard reports live traffic sources, viewed pages and completed goals; the reader can inspect that reporting in the public demo.
emails.belief_shift: Before: a cookie-free analytics option may sound privacy-compatible but too abstract to assess. After: Plausible has a visible reporting interface the team can inspect against its own core analytics requirements.
must_not_say: Do not claim that adopting Plausible automatically removes every consent-banner, DPIA, legal or procurement obligation.
Do not describe Plausible as legally certified, independently certified, ISO 27001 certified or SOC 2 certified.
Do not claim a guaranteed uptime SLA.
Do not claim that Plausible avoids procurement or is free.
Do not say Plausible fixes GA4's reporting interface, multiple-view, exploration or sub-property limitations.
Do not claim Plausible has more generous API quotas than GA4 or that it removes API constraints.
Do not claim Plausible reconciles, imports or compares historical Universal Analytics and GA4 datasets.
Do not claim Plausible reduces storage costs or is cheaper for a national-scale government site.
Do not promise to solve P5: character or field-length limits on collected data are not established.
Do not imply user-level tracking, deep attribution or unrestricted raw event data.
Do not introduce SSO, Enterprise features, pricing, trial terms, customer logos or unrelated security controls into this email.
Do not state or imply that every recipient currently uses GA4, has suffered a failed migration or has encountered the documented GOV.UK problems.
emails.objection: Will a tool that does not use cookies or collect personal data still show the basic traffic, page and goal information the team needs?
emails.tone: Matter-of-fact, concise and suitable for a public-sector reader; confident without making legal assurances.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Plausible's core dashboard is relevant enough to enter the team's formal analytics, privacy and procurement assessment.
emails.next_step_value: The public demo lets the reader inspect a working dashboard showing live traffic sources, pages being viewed and goals being met without creating an account.
emails.next_step_limit: The demo does not establish fit for department-specific reporting, API workloads, historical-data requirements, accessibility review, DPIA approval, procurement, SSO or production implementation.
emails.subject_strategy: Connect the reader's cookie-free analytics requirement to a concrete dashboard inspection. Signal practical evaluation rather than promise compliance, savings or a complete GA4 replacement.

raw_plan.voice_notes: Use short, declarative paragraphs and Plausible's plain vocabulary. Avoid hype, legal shorthand such as 'fully compliant,' and unsupported claims that no consent banner is ever required.

events.body:
You can inspect Plausible Analytics’ live dashboard before deciding whether it belongs in a formal privacy and reporting assessment. It shows where traffic comes from, which pages are being viewed and which goals are being met.

Plausible is a web analytics service that uses no cookies and collects no personal data. It also uses no persistent identifiers or cross-site or cross-device tracking, and does not reuse site data for other purposes.

The public demo provides a working view of its core reporting without requiring an account. Your team can compare the dashboard with its own requirements before committing time to a fuller assessment.

It is a concrete way to judge whether cookie-free analytics can provide the basic traffic, page and goal information your services need.

events.body:
Plausible uses no cookies or persistent identifiers. It collects no personal data and does not track visitors across sites or devices.

Plausible Analytics is a privacy-friendly web analytics tool with a dashboard for live traffic sources, pages being viewed and goals being met. Site data is not used for other purposes.

The public demo lets you inspect that reporting without creating an account. You can compare the visible dashboard with your team’s core reporting requirements before deciding whether a formal privacy, analytics and procurement assessment is worthwhile.

That makes the first decision concrete: whether the core dashboard merits closer assessment by your team.

Problem context: GA4's changed definitions of core concepts (such as sessions) and its batching of events make it hard for GOV.UK to compare GA4 data with their historical Universal Analytics data and to plot user journeys.; source: https://gds.blog.gov.uk/2023/03/27/sharing-data-and-lessons-from-our-google-analytics-4-upgrade/
Problem context: GOV.UK expects GA4's larger daily data tables to increase their data storage costs compared with Universal Analytics.; source: https://gds.blog.gov.uk/2023/03/27/sharing-data-and-lessons-from-our-google-analytics-4-upgrade/
Problem context: Character limits on data sent to GA4 constrain what GOV.UK is able to collect.; source: https://gds.blog.gov.uk/2023/03/27/sharing-data-and-lessons-from-our-google-analytics-4-upgrade/

For analytics intended to operate without a consent banner, reporting usefulness and privacy suitability are separate questions.

Plausible Analytics is a web analytics service. Its published documentation states that it uses no cookies, collects no personal data, uses no persistent identifiers and does not track visitors across sites or devices.

Its security page provides a route to its public privacy policy, data policy, data processing agreement and compliance documentation for a separate privacy assessment.

The public demo answers the reporting question without an account. It shows live traffic sources, pages being viewed and goals being met.

Inspect those reports to decide whether Plausible’s dashboard is relevant enough to justify a formal assessment.
